docs.purpose: A plain row browser over whatever table a chosen pipeline step writes to. The operator arrives with a step already selected (usually from the freshness timeline's inspect link), pages through the rows fifty at a time, and can narrow them by typing a field name and value then pressing apply. Rows that carry a permit identity link straight through to the per-record inspector. It is read-only.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/admin/pipeline/step-output`. Behind that contract, the data comes from `information_schema.columns` and `pg_class`.
docs.under_126: **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the LIST renderer (a collection with declared pagination, recycling and empty/offline states), reading by reference: `/api/admin/pipeline/step-output`. Its `owns.components[]` declares `src/components/admin/StepOutputInspector.tsx`.

versioning.why: The payload is whatever columns the target table has, chosen at request time from the manifest, so there is no fixed shape for a consumer to depend on.

inputs.why: One contract; the table it reads is chosen at request time from the step manifest rather than named by the client.

outputs.why: GET only, inside a transaction that issues SELECTs alone under a 15s statement timeout.

state.why: One TanStack query under the root provider; the slug comes from the URL search params, not from a store.

staleness.why: 60s staleTime under the root persisted cache — long enough that a step finishing mid-inspection is not reflected until a refetch, which is the point: it is a row browser, not a monitor.

session.why: There is no admin Postgres role: classifyRoute sends every /admin/* path down the admin arm, and the real boundary is verifyAdminAuth reading profiles.is_admin on the route. It verifies on the first line and then logs the acting uid with the slug, table, limit and offset as an access trail.

rls_class.why: Every reachable table is a pipeline/enrichment table — Class B by the §2 default — and the five user-owned Class-A tables are kept out by an explicit PII exclusion list rather than by policy.

checks.why: lead_views, tracked_projects, lead_analytics, notifications and notification_dispatches are excluded from the inspectable set before any query runs — a pre-render gate, because the alternative is dumping a user-owned table into an admin browser.
The read runs under SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 15000, so an unbounded browse of a 500K-row table fails fast instead of holding a connection.
A step whose table is empty must say so rather than render a headerless grid; the StepOutputInspector suite locks it.

errors.why: Every path returns the { data, error, meta } envelope with a code — badRequestZod, notFound and internalError all come from the shared helpers — and the inspector renders from it.

classes.ui: envelope error rendered above the grid
envelope error rendered above the grid

emits.why: Nothing here is countable: the route writes a structured access log line naming the uid and slug (a log, not an event or a ledger row) and neither the page nor the inspector imports captureEvent.
breadcrumbs: step-output fetched (uid, slug, table, limit, offset, filtered)

offers.why: An internal operator tool renders no sponsored placement; no offers/placements table is reached from any file it owns.

metering.why: Nothing here is billable or quota-bearing: no usage_events / ledger write is reached from this surface or its contracts.

config.why: It reads no logic_variables row; the allow-list and the PII exclusions are declared in manifest-utils.ts against scripts/manifest.json.

sharing.why: /api/admin/pipeline/step-output has one caller — this page, reached by the FreshnessTimeline "Inspect output" link rather than from the /admin tile grid.

limitations.what: The governing spec cannot be named
limitations.measured: Both the page and the inspector carry a SPEC LINK to docs/specs/01-pipeline/26_*.md §3.1 and no file matching 26_* exists in that directory; neither file appears in any system-map row, and the only live references treat the inspector as DEFERRED (Spec 49:255) or as a form-pattern precedent (Spec 33:79).

limitations.what: The projection is a table-level allow-list, not a column-level whitelist
limitations.measured: Rows are returned with every column of the target table; the only filter is the manifest allow-list plus the five-table PII exclusion.

limitations.what: touch_target_min_px has no legal answer for a desktop-only admin page
limitations.measured: The schema allows only UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44, and nothing in this surface declares a 44px floor (grep for min-h-[44 / h-11 over its owned files returns nothing).
limitations.check_id: none — vocabulary gap, escalated per Spec 128 §4

notes: Spec marked unmeasured because the SPEC LINK headers on BOTH the page and StepOutputInspector.tsx cite `docs/specs/01-pipeline/26_*.md Sec 3.1`, and no file matching 26_* exists in docs/specs/01-pipeline/ (26_admin_dashboard.md lives in 02-web-admin and contains no step-output content). Neither file appears in any system-map row. The only live references are 01-pipeline/49_data_completeness_profiling.md line 255, which lists 'the Step-Output row Inspector' as DEFERRED to a design brief, and 33_web_admin_engineering_protocol.md line 79, which cites it only as a form-pattern precedent. Reached by link, not from the /admin tile grid. identity.owner is UNRESEARCHED estate-wide: no owner registry exists in the tree, so naming one would be an invention rather than a measurement. a11y.touch_target_min_px is UNRESEARCHED because its vocabulary (UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44) has no member for a desktop-only admin page that declares no floor.

programme.why: An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.
